stops.note: a Germanic personal name, Latinised as Guido, borne by Guido of Arezzo, who devised the musical staff around 1030
French turned the Germanic w- into gu-, as in guerre from werra; the Normans brought the name to England
Guy Fawkes was caught guarding gunpowder under the House of Lords on 5 November 1605; effigies burnt on Bonfire Night were called 'guys'
from a grotesquely dressed figure to any odd-looking person, then simply 'a man' in American usage

current_meaning: a man; (plural) people of either sex
